title: the_inheritance_clause_my_uncle_wrote
display_title: My uncle rewrote his will over a Minecraft speedrun world record he didn't believe was real
share_line: Send this to anyone whose family never once took their hobby seriously.
beats: My uncle (61M) wrote me out of his will over a Minecraft world record he swore I faked.
I'd just posted a verified sub-9-minute speedrun, and at Thanksgiving he called it 'computer magic for children' in front of the whole family.
Two weeks later my aunt let it slip: he'd amended his will, splitting my share between my cousins because I 'wasted my twenties on a toy.'

So I mailed him the seed, the run files, and a signed letter from the verification team confirming it was legitimate — plus a printout of what that world record now licenses for in tournament sponsorships.
Turns out 'computer magic for children' paid my rent for a year, and his favorite grandson's college fund could've used a slice of it.
He called eight months later asking to be added back to my beneficiary list — I read him the same line he gave me: 'It's just a toy, Uncle Ray.' Was I wrong?
